subject: ventures/custom-farm-rate-calculator
professional: an extension farm-management specialist who writes machinery-cost and custom-rate budgets (the Iowa State Ag Decision Maker A3-24/A3-29 kind), checking first: the field-capacity equation and field efficiency, ownership cost spread over annual hours, the operating-cost items (fuel, repairs, lubrication, labor with its 1.1-1.2 factor), what field efficiency leaves out (travel, service), and how the result compares to the regional custom rate survey

evidence.correctness: Sources the author did not write, fetched from extension.iastate.edu (HTTP 200 through the proxy): Ag Decision Maker A3-24 'Estimating the Field Capacity of Farm Machines' (sha256 81e35246...), A3-29 'Estimating Farm Machinery Costs' (f05c93a9...), A3-10 '2026 Iowa Farm Custom Rate Survey' (f5785e14...). Probe script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/bfc40cd0-35aa-5329-b7a8-571e88aa5cb8/scratchpad/custom-farm-rate-calculator/probes.mjs imports the shipped calc.mjs. A3-24's three GPS-era examples (45 ft x 4.5 mph x 80% = 19.6; 60 x 6.0 x 85% = 37.1; 120 x 12 x 92% = 160.5 ac/hr) give 19.64, 37.09, 160.58 (pass, rounding only). Hand recomputation of the defaults (cap 12.2727 ac/hr, 13.037 h, total 2,610.01, break-even 16.31, bill 16.31/0.85 = 19.19) and the 100-hour column (4,800.24, 35.30, +84%) match the tool and the guide page; headless Chrome on index.html renders '$19.19/ac', 'about 13.0 hrs at 12.3 ac/hr'. A3-29's tractor per-hour example (own 32,256/400 = 80.64, fuel 0.044 x 300 hp x $3.40 = 44.88, repairs 6.67, lube 0.15 x fuel = 6.73, labor $25 x 1.1 = 27.50; total 166.42/h) fed in gives 163.92/h: ownership and fuel exact, the 2.50 gap is the labor factor the tool omits (partial). Margin as share of price: cost 1,000 at 40% -> 1,666.67 (pass). Wrong numbers from input handling: a blank field becomes 0 with no error (Number('') = 0): emptying Annual ownership cost on the live page shows '$8.45/ac' with no error instead of $19.19; a zero-profit job row is dropped from the season count, so jobs 460/310/0 give average 385 and 14 more jobs instead of 256.67 and 21.
evidence.completeness: Claims checked on the page (headless Chrome --dump-dom over python3 -m http.server): one-job pricing renders every breakdown row ($2610.01 total, $16.31/ac break-even); season section renders $770.00 total, $5230.00 gap, 14 more jobs (hand: 6000-770 = 5230, ceil(5230/385) = 14); invalid input hides stale results (page.test.mjs); guide page and vs-survey page exist and link both ways; usage opt-out button and DNT/GPC wording present. No TODOs or stubs; sitemap and sibling-link tests pass. Everything the README says it does runs end to end.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/custom-farm-rate-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 48 tests, 48 pass, 0.14 s. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 1 caught (8.25 -> 8.5), 5 SURVIVED: labor not multiplied by hours, fuel not multiplied by hours, labor dropped from totalCost, ownership cost halved, Math.ceil -> Math.round in incomeGap. No test pins a dollar output of calculate(); calc tests are directional (a > b, > 0). The guide test titled 'matches calc.mjs exactly' (page.test.mjs:95) computes calculate() but then only greps the HTML for hard-coded strings ($19.19, $2,610.01), so the engine can change without failing it. The ceil test (calc.test.mjs:83) uses 600/300 = 2 exactly, so round and ceil agree.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (146 lines), index.html script (lines 96-167), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Small, pure engine imported by the page, explicit bounds with readable errors, margin < 100 guarded. Defects: number() treats '' as 0 (calc.mjs:39) so a blank required field is a silent zero; effectiveHourlyEarnings is computed (calc.mjs:111) and never shown; header says 'Two distinct calculations' then lists three (calc.mjs:4-18); money() prints no thousands separator ('$2610.01', '$5230.00', index.html:100) while the guide page uses '$2,610.01'. Acceptable for a senior reviewer with those fixes requested.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty and 'not agronomic, tax, financial, or business advice' on index.html footer, both content pages and README (page.test.mjs asserts it). Guide page numbers (112.00, 280.00, 602.31, 1,460.15, 3,650.37, 2,610.01, 4,800.24, 19.19, 35.30, '84%') all reproduce by hand. Privacy claims match the code (no fetch; usage.mjs local counter). The result note discloses no hauling, drying or second machine. Small overclaim: calc.mjs:20-22 says 8.25 is 'the same one land-grant extension custom-rate surveys use'; the survey (A3-10) reports charges, the formula is from the field-capacity file (A3-24/ASABE EP496). vs-survey page says surveys 'report one job's average' and does not name or misquote any survey (pass). Served copy (`node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs custom-farm-rate-calculator`): no placeholder or retired origin, so the github.io links in source llms.txt are rewritten at deploy (not filed).
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a custom operator pricing a 160-acre job with a 30-ft machine. The tool gives a defensible cost floor and makes the utilisation point well. Gaps hit in the first hour: no travel/road time or setup between customers (A3-24 says field efficiency excludes travel to and from the field, daily service and repairs), no labor factor, units only per acre (balers price per bale, hauling per bushel or mile), no input for the going survey rate to compare against although two pages sell that comparison, tractor and implement must share one hours-per-year figure, and the season table asks the user to copy each job's profit by hand. Usable for a first estimate on per-acre field work, not as the operator's rate sheet. Nearest tools: ISU AgDM machinery cost spreadsheets (A3-29 companion) and the A3-10 survey itself.
evidence.domain: Against ISU AgDM A3-24 and A3-29 (2026 revisions) and ASABE EP496.3 as cited there: EFC = W x S x FE / 8.25 exact (pass); ownership cost per hour = annual ownership / annual hours, as A3-29 (pass); margin as a share of price, stated (pass). Departs: labor charged on field hours only, A3-29 says labor hours exceed machine hours by 10-20% (x1.1 or 1.2); lubrication (15% of fuel, A3-29) not prompted, only foldable into repairs; travel, service and setup time not modelled though A3-24 excludes them from field efficiency; tractor and implement ownership share one hours denominator, A3-29 costs them separately; no fuel estimate aid (0.044 gal per max PTO hp, A3-29). A specialist would accept the method as a simplified budget and ask for labor factor, travel time and separate tractor/implement hours before signing off.

defects.what: Five of six seeded bugs in the cost engine survive the 48 tests (labor or fuel not scaled by hours, labor dropped from total cost, ownership halved, ceil -> round). No test pins a dollar output of calculate(); the calc tests are directional only.

The guide-page test titled 'matches calc.mjs exactly' calls calculate() but then only greps hard-coded strings in the HTML, so the engine and the published worked example can drift apart without a failure (the labor-dropped mutant survives).

A blank cost field is treated as 0 with no error (Number('') === 0): emptying Annual ownership cost on the live page shows $8.45/ac instead of $19.19/ac with the error line hidden; blank fuel price, fuel burn, repairs, labor and margin are likewise silent zeros. A user who skips a field gets an underpriced rate.

Labor is charged on field hours only, and travel, setup and service time between customers are not modelled; ISU A3-29 says labor hours exceed field machine time by 10-20% and A3-24 says field efficiency excludes travel to and from the field. Understates the floor for a custom operator, whose road time is a real cost. Not disclosed in the result note.

Season table ignores zero-profit rows ('Blank or zero rows are ignored'), so a break-even job is dropped from the job count and inflates the average: 460/310/0 gives average $385 and 14 more jobs instead of $256.67 and 21.

Scope gaps a custom operator hits: only per-acre pricing (balers price per bale, hauling per bushel or mile); no input for the going survey rate to compare against, though two pages are about that comparison; tractor and implement share one hours-per-year denominator (A3-29 costs them separately); lubrication (about 15% of fuel, A3-29) not prompted.
Comment credits the 8.25 field-capacity constant to 'land-grant extension custom-rate surveys'; the surveys (e.g. ISU A3-10) report charges, the equation comes from ASABE EP496 / ISU A3-24.

Craft: effectiveHourlyEarnings is computed and never shown; the header says 'Two distinct calculations' and lists three; money() has no thousands separator ('$2610.01') while the guide page writes '$2,610.01'.

verdict: A small, honest per-acre cost-floor calculator whose arithmetic is right and whose tests would not notice if it stopped being right. Against Iowa State AgDM A3-24 and A3-29 (2026, fetched from extension.iastate.edu), field capacity matches all three published examples, ownership cost per hour and fuel match the A3-29 tractor example exactly, and the default job and the guide page's 250-vs-100-hour table reproduce by hand to the cent ($19.19 vs $35.30/ac). Weaknesses: 5 of 6 seeded engine bugs survive the 48 tests, including dropping labor from total cost, because no test pins a dollar output and the guide test greps hard-coded strings; a blank cost field silently prices as zero ($8.45 instead of $19.19 with ownership blank); labor ignores the A3-29 1.1-1.2 factor and travel time; zero-profit season rows are dropped. Disclaimer and privacy claims hold; served llms.txt is clean. Does not meet the bar (verification 1); finished (completeness 3). Fixable in one session: reject blank inputs, pin dollar outputs in tests and compute the guide table from calc.mjs, add travel hours and a labor factor.
